title: Early screening of sales opportunities for conflicts before a pitch advances
problem: Pitching for work that later fails conflicts checks wastes pursuit effort and embarrasses the firm.
approach: Intapp says its conflicts product can screen opportunities before they advance to formal review (vendor-published, announced capability).
For ChatGPT Enterprise users, the Celeste plug-in is described as sourcing opportunities on work already cleared for conflicts.
Formal conflicts review still follows before acceptance. No outcome figure is published.

title: AI-prefilled acceptance requests with role-based risk summaries for reviewers
problem: Fee earners re-key client and matter details into acceptance forms, and reviewers read long requests to find conflicts, anti-money-laundering and jurisdiction issues.
approach: Intapp says Celeste prefills requests from emails and files, validates entries, and writes summaries highlighting conflicts, money-laundering risk, jurisdiction and strategic fit.
The requester confirms prefilled fields before submission; reviewers approve or escalate the request.
No outcome figure published (vendor-published); described as an announced capability.

title: AI agent that searches conflicts, triages hits and drafts clearance summaries
problem: Conflicts analysts build searches, read long hit lists and write up each clearance decision, while volume rises and client history often sits outside the conflicts database.
approach: Intapp says Celeste builds the search strategy, triages high-risk hits, drafts a clearance summary and keeps monitoring data sources for new issues.
BakerHostetler is named as an early adopter; Intapp says relevant matters surface 'in minutes rather than hours' (vendor-published, no measured study).
Experts review triaged hits before clearance; a partner or risk counsel decides on waivers and screens.

title: Small-firm conflicts-check agent that maps corporate families and fuzzy-matches names
problem: A small firm clears conflicts with a spreadsheet and partner memory, missing relationships hidden behind different entity names or corporate parents.
approach: A four-stage agent ingests matter details, maps corporate hierarchies, runs fuzzy and opposing-party searches, and scores each potential match by risk.
The builder reports conflicts-check time fell from 2-3 hours to 8 minutes per matter (self-reported; unnamed 14-attorney firm).
Direct and related-entity flags go to the responsible partner for the legal call; no-match results are auto-approved with an audit trail.
who: Unnamed small US law firm (builder's account)

title: Agent pre-screens lateral hires for conflicts and prepares clearance
problem: Lateral hires bring client relationships that must be checked for conflicts before the hire is made, and confidential information has to be handled carefully.
approach: Intapp says Celeste can run an end-to-end lateral hire lifecycle: candidate research, conflicts pre-screening, clearance preparation and onboarding.
Intapp's intake product also offers lateral candidates a secure portal to share confidential details.
Announcement only; no outcome figure is published (vendor-published) and human checkpoints are not described in the sources.

title: AI-written, sourced due-diligence report that routes new clients by risk
problem: Every new client needs money-laundering and bribery screening, so analysts spend hours on low-risk clients while the few risky ones wait in the same queue.
approach: Pinsent Masons co-developed with Xapien an LLM-powered tool that writes a sourced report on money-laundering, bribery and ESG risks.
Low-risk reports pass with minimal oversight, medium-risk go to the AML team, and high-risk need further verification or partner consultation.
Pinsent Masons expects low-risk clients cleared in hours rather than days, and a report in around 15 minutes (expectation).

title: Idea: AI agent screens news coverage of prospective clients (research prototype)
problem: Keyword-based adverse-media screening (searching news for negative coverage of a client) produces many false positives, and hybrid systems need extensive manual review.
approach: This is an idea, not a deployment: an LLM agent searches the web and scores adverse media, with a written justification.
A December 2025 University of Luxembourg paper presents an open-source version aimed at financial institutions' compliance; no outcome figure is published.
An analyst reviews the score and justification.

title: Risk-based acceptance workflow with scoring, routing, audit trail and generated engagement letters
problem: Acceptance run on email chains, paper and legacy systems takes days to weeks, gives partners no status visibility and tempts lawyers to bypass the process.
approach: A configured platform routes approvals by risk score, jurisdiction, service line and counterparty, connects checks, and keeps an audit trail.
Intapp's case study says BDO Canada handles over 5,000 acceptances a month, a 38% improvement (vendor-published). Sandberg Phoenix reports triple the matters.
Loeb & Loeb says weeks-long work is usually done in hours (vendor-published).
Partners and risk teams still approve; the case studies do not isolate any AI feature.
who: BDO Canada, Sandberg Phoenix, Loeb & Loeb

title: Engagement letters generated from approved intake data and routed for signature
problem: Engagement letters get delayed or missed when intake is manual, and scope, terms and client-specific AI wording vary.
approach: Intapp says its intake platform turns approved intake data into engagement letters and routes them for review and signature, enforcing firm policy.
Loeb & Loeb says letters 'could no longer be overlooked or delayed' once intake fields were mandatory (workflow, not AI; vendor-published).
Review and signature routing applies; one bar source calls lawyer approval of an agent's autonomous actions, such as sending a letter, prudent.

title: AI reads client outside counsel guidelines and enforces them at intake
problem: Each client sends its own outside counsel guidelines, which are slow and risky to manage in documents, and teams cannot quickly answer questions about payment or security terms across clients.
approach: Fredrikson & Byron's risk counsel says the AI makes a first pass categorising each obligation in a client's guidelines; she confirms it.
Staff can ask a generative AI feature about client terms in Teams; Intapp says terms appear in intake, conflicts and time entry.
She says she can pull terms across clients much faster; no figure given (vendor-published).

title: Idea: register of client AI restrictions and consents, checked at matter opening
problem: Clients are adding AI rules to outside counsel guidelines and engagement letters, such as consent, approved tools and no client data in public models, and permitted tools differ by client.
approach: Idea, not a deployment: capture client AI terms as structured obligations at intake and check each AI tool against them.
The firm would also record which tool touched which matter. A vendor guide (Layer3 Labs) proposes it.
Intapp announced a Celeste plug-in for ChatGPT Enterprise to check work against outside counsel guidelines.

title: Ethical walls extended to AI assistants so they only see permitted matters
problem: AI assistants that search firm content can reach matters a person behind an ethical wall may not see; governance protocols have historically not extended into AI platforms and agents.
approach: Nelson Mullins' applications manager says with Intapp Walls she can point Microsoft Copilot where she wants and it pulls only permitted matters.
Intapp and Harvey announced plans to sync wall policies with Harvey's access and sharing controls.
Risk or IT teams monitor access reports and blocked attempts. No test result or incident count is published.

title: Ongoing re-screening of clients after acceptance, with alerts when risk changes
problem: Risk checks happen at onboarding, then clients change owners or face sanctions; a summary of a 2025 regulator report says 92% of firms screen new clients, 79% re-check existing ones.
approach: Intapp says its intake platform alerts when ownership, sanctions status, litigation exposure or jurisdictional risk shifts, and triggers reviews at risk thresholds.
Celeste is described as continuously monitoring integrated data sources for conflicts. No outcome figure is published (vendor-published); announced.
The risk team triages alerts and decides on strategic review or exit.

title: In-house legal front door that routes, completes and logs business requests
problem: In-house teams get a stream of incomplete requests, and business teams stall or proceed without legal input and take on risk legal never sees.
approach: In-house, vendor-described and piloting: Legora's Intake agent reads each request, asks for missing details, routes it and drafts from playbooks.
A lawyer reviews every piece of work by default; routine pre-approved requests such as a standard NDA can bypass review.
Harvey's Intake routes requests to approved agents or lawyers with an audit trail.
